name: trace.matrix
title: Show traceability matrix
summary: Traceability matrix of a selection: one row per element in list order, one column per relation kind and direction that occurs, each cell the elements at the other end with outdated and missing marks; per column how many rows have a link. Gaps only where the metamodel sets a minimum (limits with min): such a column also gives how many of the rows it applies to meet it, and their share, and marks the rows below it. One page of rows at a time. With evidence locations also each requirement's test cases and verification status, and the degree.

selection.description: The rows: every element the selection selects, as `element.list` selects them (every part given must hold, SR-101 AK2). In a variant view (`selection.view`, or the view of the saved filter) a link whose other end the view does not hold (SR-040, SR-043: also a core requirement the variant excludes or replaces) is left out of the cells and the counts, as `trace.neighbourhood` leaves it out of its walk.

sort.description: As in `element.list`: the rows are in the order `element.list` gives for the same `selection` and `sort` (SR-125 AK1). Without `sort`, the sort of the saved filter in `selection.filter`. `hierarchy` first makes the rows the derivation tree and gives each row its `depth`.

kinds.description: Keys of the relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to make columns of. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. Without `kinds`, the columns are the relation kinds of the metamodel (Beziehungsarten, D-043, D-037): relation properties such as the package and the validity are their own built-in meanings (D-012) and form a column only when named here; inline references are no relation kind and never form a column.

limit.description: Rows of the page; `total` counts all.

offset.description: Rows skipped before the page, in the order of the list.

columns.description: One column per relation kind and direction that occurs in the whole selection (SR-125 AK2), not only on the page: a kind or direction no row has makes no column, except the `out` column of a relation kind whose limits set a minimum (`min` of 1 or more) for the type of a row, which is there even when no row has such a relation (SR-153, spec question #838 Q1). Order: relation kinds in the order of the metamodel, then properties of kind `relation` in property order; per key `out` before `in`. `type` says what a column holds and so the shape of its cells; every column is `relation`. The evidence columns (SR-126) are no column type: their header is `evidence` and their cells are `rows[].testCases` and `rows[].verification`, so a reader of `columns` and `cells` needs no other shape.

type.description: The column holds relations: its cell in each row is an array of relations (`data-export#/$defs/relation`) of `kind` and `direction`. The evidence columns are `evidence`, `rows[].testCases` and `rows[].verification`, not a column type.

kind.description: Key of the relation kind, or of the property of kind `relation`.

property.description: `kind` is the key of a property of kind `relation`, not of a relation kind.

meaning.description: The meaning of the relation kind; left out for a kind without a meaning and for a property.

direction.description: `out`: the relations the row element's file stores. `in`: the relations of other elements that point at it.

name.description: For `out`, the `name` of the kind (e.g. Derives from); for `in`, its `inverse-name` (e.g. Derived by), the `name` when it has none. A name can be the same for both directions (Distinct from): `direction` tells them apart.

count.description: How many rows of the whole selection have at least one relation in this column (SR-125 AK3, SR-153 AK2), whatever state its other end is in; a relation to a missing target counts. With a view, the relations the cells show. 0 only for a column with minima that no row has a relation in.

expected.description: SR-153 AK1: only on the `out` column of a relation kind whose limits set a minimum (`min` of 1 or more) for the type of a row of the whole selection: how many rows have such a minimum (spec question #838 Q2). Rows of an unknown type or with a status the metamodel marks invalid have none (as SR-152). Left out on every other column, which has no gap and no share (SR-153 AK2).

met.description: SR-153 AK1: with `expected`, how many of those rows meet all minima of the kind, counted as `hint.list` counts for `relation.too-few` (SR-152): a relation counts when its target is one element of a known type within the minimum's target type; with a view, only a target that applies in it. A row whose count an unreachable target leaves open is not met and no gap (spec question #838 Q5).

share.description: SR-153 AK1: with `expected`, `met` divided by `expected`. Left out on a column without a minimum (SR-153 AK2).

rows.description: The page: one row per element of the list, in its order (SR-125 AK1).

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element.

identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

depth.description: Only when `sort` starts with `hierarchy`: the depth of the element in the derivation tree, as `element.list` gives it in `tree`.

testCases.description: SR-126 AK1, AK2: only with `evidence`, on a row whose type has the meaning `requirement` and that applies in its view. The test cases that name the requirement, with their verification executions that hold in the view of `evidence` (`trace.chain` shows the same test cases in the same view), by class name then name; an empty array when it has none: a gap (AK2). Records without a test case (inspection, analysis, a manual record without `test-case`) are not here; they count for `verification` only (spec question ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#528 Q3). The chain and `evidence.list` give every execution.

name.description: The JUnit `name`, or the `test-case` of the Markdown records.

className.description: The JUnit `classname`; left out for a test case of Markdown records.

executed.description: The test case has at least one execution of this requirement in the view (SR-033 AK3).

last.description: The last execution: the newest execution of this requirement in the view, of any version, with result, date, item and version; its record file (`repository`, `file`, `line`) is the evidence of a JUnit execution. Left out when `executed` is false.

mark.description: How the cell is marked (AK2; spec questions ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#528 Q1, Q2 and ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#593 Q2), the first that holds: `not-executed` when `executed` is false; `outdated` when `last` is of another version than the requirement's current one, or its current version is not known; `failed` when `last` failed. Left out when the last execution passed for the current version.

verification.description: SR-126 AK1, AK3: only with `evidence`, on a row whose type has the meaning `requirement` and that applies in its view. Its verification status in the view of `evidence`, one entry, the same as `element.get` and `evidence.status` give for that view: `indirect` when it is verified through its children (AK3).

cells.description: One cell per entry of `columns`, in the same order; a cell takes its shape from the type of its column. For `relation`, an array of the relations of the row element in the column's `kind` and `direction`, each with `shortId` and `title` of the other end when it is available (SR-125 AK2), and an empty array when it has none. An empty cell is no gap by itself: `gaps` names the gaps (SR-153). Outgoing relations come in the order of the file, incoming ones in the order of the incoming index (store order). A relation to an older version of its target is `outdated`, one to a target that is not there has `targetState: "missing"` (SR-125 AK4); for an incoming relation, `outdated` means its source stores an older version of the row element and `currentVersion` is the row element's.

gaps.description: SR-153 AK1: the minima of the row that its cells undershoot, one entry per minimum, in column order and then metamodel order; a cell is a gap when an entry names its column. Only `out` columns of relation kinds whose limits set a minimum for the row's type; a cell can hold relations and be a gap (to a missing target, or to an element of another type). Counted as `expected` and `met` count. Left out when the row has none.

column.description: The index of the column in `columns`, and so of the cell in `cells`.

targetType.description: The target type of the minimum.

count.description: The relations that count for the minimum, as `relation.too-few` gives `count`.

min.description: The minimum, the `min` of the limit (the `limit` of `relation.too-few`; not the page size `limit` of the input).

total.description: The number of rows of the whole selection.

incomplete.description: The selection is incomplete (SR-006 AK2), or the workspace file lists a repository that is not on this machine: relations of elements there that point at a row cannot be seen, and its elements may belong to the selection. With `evidence`, also when an evidence location lies in such a repository: its records are not seen (SR-006 AK2).

evidence.description: The header of the evidence columns (SR-126): given when the workspace file names an evidence location, the metamodel is valid and the selection holds an element whose type has the meaning `requirement` (spec question ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#593 Q1); then every requirement row of the page that applies in `view` has `testCases` and `verification`. Other rows have neither (a requirement valid only in variants, without a view): not applicable, no gap. Left out otherwise, and the output is the one without evidence (SR-125).

view.description: The one view of the test cases, the status and the degree: the selection's view, else its saved filter's, else the core (as `evidence.degree`; spec questions ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#593, ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#592 Q1). `element.get` and `evidence.status` give every view.

degree.description: SR-126 AK4: the verification degree of the whole selection in `view`, with the count per status, not of the page only; the same as `evidence.degree` gives for the same selection (SR-037).

names.description: The elements that `evidence` and the rows' `verification` name by UUID only, each once in the order first named: the variant of the view and the missing children (`missingChildren`), so a reader names them by short ID, identifier and title (ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#588). Left out when they name none.
